$what: Provenance of aurora-effects-preset.schema.json — empyrean's CONTRACT schema for the wave-2 RASTER PRESET document (bands), vendored into Aurora beside the codec that validates against it. preset.ts imports the .json directly; this sidecar records where those bytes came from, and test/formats/effects-preset-schema-drift.test.ts reads `empyrean.blob` from here as its pin of record.
$why_a_sidecar_and_not_a_test_constant: The scene schema's pin lived as a const in one test AND as prose in two other files, and the prose copies went three re-pins stale without anything going red, because nothing hashes a comment. That lesson was applied when the scene pin moved here on 2026-08-29; this file is born with it. The hash lives HERE, once, and the test reads it.
$why_vendored: Aurora's core must validate from a lone clone, inside a git worktree (where ../../empyrean is not where it is from master), and in a packaged Electron build that ships no sibling repo. A path-probe design would degrade to 'schema not found -> skip validation', which is the loud-on-unmeasurable failure this suite is not allowed to have. The cost of vendoring is staleness; the drift gate is the payment.
$this_document_is_not_a_scene: A BAND IS NOT A SCENE FIELD. A scene is a parallax_config; the raster program is a channel of an EffectsPreset, bound per SECTION. A `bands` key on a scene file is refused by the scene loader's closed-schema path, deliberately. These are two schemas and two directories, and conflating them is the failure this whole sidecar pair exists to make impossible.

aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.json_schema_subset: This schema is the first committed contract schema to put `unevaluatedProperties: false` beside an in-place applicator — at $defs.band.properties.on, where `oneOf: [{required:[cram]},{required:[pal_region]}]` spells the exactly-one-arm rule. json-schema-subset.ts refused that combination outright. The refusal was a FALSE POSITIVE here (a `required`-only branch contributes no property annotations, so the additionalProperties equivalence holds exactly), and it was narrowed to a PROVER, `contributesPropertyAnnotations`, that clears a branch only when every keyword in it is on a whitelist of provably-inert ones. $ref/$dynamicRef stay an unconditional refusal because their value is a string this evaluator does not follow.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.why_a_whitelist: The failure this evaluator exists to prevent is silently ACCEPTING what the real schema rejects. A blacklist is wrong by default on every keyword nobody thought of; a whitelist is right by default and merely inconvenient when the schema grows.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.type_arrays_12aecd5: The 12aecd5 amendment spelled `cycles` as `"type": ["array", "null"]` — the first type ARRAY in a committed contract schema. json-schema-subset.ts refused type arrays inside validateNode, i.e. only on a node a DOCUMENT reached; `type` was already an implemented keyword NAME, so the keyword-coverage gate stayed GREEN while the first document carrying `cycles` threw UnsupportedSchemaError. Two edits: (1) `type` now accepts a list of implemented type names, meaning any-of, refused by name in assertSupported before any value is seen; (2) a whole-schema walker, `assertSchemaSupported`, runs the per-node check over every node reachable or not, and both drift gates call it — because a keyword NAME can be implemented while a VALUE SHAPE of it is not, and only a walk sees the shape.
aurora_edits_this_vendoring_forced.nothing_forced_at_d36d704: The patch_world_ys / patch_motion amendment forced NO edit to json-schema-subset.ts, and that is a MEASURED result, not an assumption: the keyword census, the whole-schema walk (assertSchemaSupported) and the vectors were all run against the newly vendored bytes before this line was written. Every construct the amendment uses was already implemented and already exercised — `$ref` inside a `oneOf` branch (variants' null-slot shape), a bare `not: {const: N}` (the scene schema's drift.rate hole), `minimum`/`maximum`, `maxItems`, and `unevaluatedProperties: false` beside plain `properties`/`required` (patch_motion_entry, anchor_sweep). The one shape worth naming because it looks like the 6664b61 false positive and is NOT one: `$defs.patch_motion_entry` carries `unevaluatedProperties: false` with NO in-place applicator beside it, so the additionalProperties equivalence holds without needing the `contributesPropertyAnnotations` prover at all.
